“Modernity and the Ozarks,” topic of fifth installment of OHRC Conversation Series – Celebrating 250 years of America in the Ozarks

By
James Hurtt
-
August 9, 2026
Facebook
X
Pinterest
WhatsApp
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 2:30
    Instaread

              WEST PLAINS, Mo. – Modernity is the fifth and final installment to “Celebrating 250 years of America in the Ozarks” conversation series. Free to attend and open to the public, this event is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m., Thursday, Aug. 13, at the Ozarks Heritage Research Center (OHRC) located inside Garnett Library, 304 W. Trish Knight St., in West Plains. The featured conversation facilitator for this event will be Carol Silvey.

    “Modernity and the Ozarks” will be advertised and discussed on Wednesday, Aug. 12, from 12:15 – 12:45 p.m., on the KUKU 100.3 FM radio show, “High Noon in American History with Cowboy Rick.”

    Advertisement

    Attendees will be invited to share stories and thoughts about how the Ozarks are part of the American tapestry. Tools and resources of the OHRC will be highlighted as components to preserve the cultural distinctions of the Ozarks.

    More about Silvey

              Silvey is a graduate of Ava High School and received a bachelor’s degree in history education from Missouri State University (MSU) in 1964. She earned a master’s degree in educational administration from the University of Missouri.

    Silvey was employed at MSU-WP for 38 years. She was a history instructor from 1968 to 1991, then worked as a director of development until 2006.  After her departure from the campus, she served as vice president of advancement for the Community Foundation of the Ozarks and the Ozarks Medical Center Foundation.

    Silvey is widely known for her volunteerism and dedication to public service. She has served on multiple university, civic, and governmental boards and committees and has consistently supported initiatives that benefit both the campus and the broader community.

    Silvey has also received numerous honors and awards including the Business and Professional Women’s Woman of the Year Award, the West Plains Chamber of Commerce’s Volunteer of the Year and Lifetime Achievement Awards, Outstanding Rotarian for Community Service Award, Mountain Grove Chamber of Commerce’s Lifetime Achievement Award, the university’s Staff Community Service Award, Granvil Vaughan Founder’s Award and the Distinguished Staff Award. She was inducted into the Wall of Fame at MSU during a special ceremony in 2012. When Hass-Darr Hall opened in 2018, it included the Carol Silvey Student Union, a space for students to gather for studying, snacking, or relaxing.  

    For more information

    Please contact Rebekah McKinney at 417-255-7949 or RebekahMcKinney@MissouriState.edu for more information about this event as well as upcoming events held at the Garnett Library.

    Visit WP.MissouriState.edu/Ozarks for more information about OHRC news and upcoming events
